preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 100 for x in stdin.split() if x.isdigit()) and len(stdin.split()) == 2
preconditions.description: The input consists of exactly two integers n and m, each between 1 and 100 inclusive, representing the dimensions of the grid.
The total number of squares (n × m) is at least 2, ensuring the king must visit at least one non-capital square.

postconditions.description: The first line of the output is a non-negative integer k, representing the minimum number of teleporters required.

postconditions.expression: k == 0 or (k > 0 and all(len(line.split()) == 4 for line in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:k+1]))
postconditions.description: If k > 0, the next k lines each contain exactly four integers (x1, y1, x2, y2) representing teleporter placements and destinations.
The remaining lines (k+1 to k+1+nm) each contain exactly two integers representing the king's path coordinates.
The path contains exactly n × m + 1 coordinates (visiting each square once except the capital, which is visited twice).

postconditions.expression: path[0] == path[-1] == '1 1' and all(path[i] != path[j] for i in range(1, len(path)-1) for j in range(i+1, len(path)-1))
postconditions.description: The path starts and ends at (1, 1), and all other coordinates are unique (no revisits except the capital).

postconditions.expression: all(abs(int(x1) - int(x2)) + abs(int(y1) - int(y2)) <= 1 or any(line.split() == [x1, y1, x2, y2] for line in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:k+1]) for (x1, y1), (x2, y2) in zip(path[:-1], path[1:]))
postconditions.description: Each consecutive pair of coordinates in the path is either side-neighboring (Manhattan distance 1) or connected by a teleporter.

postconditions.expression: k == 0 or all(1 <= int(x) <= int(n) and 1 <= int(y) <= int(m) for line in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1:k+1] for x, y in [(line.split()[0], line.split()[1]), (line.split()[2], line.split()[3])])
postconditions.description: All teleporter coordinates (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) are within the grid bounds.
k is the minimum number of teleporters required to construct a valid path (min_k is the smallest possible k satisfying all other postconditions).
